text: Classic Chocolate Chip Cookies. Preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius and line two baking trays with parchment paper. In a large bowl, cream 115 grams of softened butter with 100 grams of brown sugar and 50 grams of white sugar until the mixture is light and fluffy. Beat in one large egg and a teaspoon of vanilla extract. In a separate bowl, whisk together 190 grams of plain flour, half a teaspoon of baking soda and a pinch of salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture and stir until just combined. Fold in 150 grams of dark chocolate chips. Scoop tablespoon-sized balls of dough onto the trays, leaving space between them because the cookies will spread. Bake for ten to twelve minutes, until the edges are golden but the centres still look slightly soft. Let the cookies cool on the tray for five minutes before moving them to a wire rack. They keep well in an airtight tin for up to a week.
label: dessert

text: Vanilla Sponge Cake. Grease and line two round cake tins and preheat the oven to 175 degrees Celsius. Beat 200 grams of soft butter with 200 grams of caster sugar for several minutes until pale. Add four eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition, then mix in two teaspoons of vanilla extract. Sift 200 grams of self-raising flour with a teaspoon of baking powder and fold it gently into the batter with a large metal spoon, keeping as much air in the mixture as possible. Add two tablespoons of milk to loosen the batter. Divide it evenly between the tins and smooth the tops. Bake for about twenty-five minutes, until the sponges are golden and spring back when pressed lightly. Cool them completely on a rack. Spread one sponge with strawberry jam and whipped cream, place the second sponge on top and dust the cake with icing sugar before serving.
label: dessert

text: Lemon Tart. Make the pastry by rubbing 100 grams of cold butter into 200 grams of flour until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs, then stir in 50 grams of icing sugar and bind with one egg yolk and a little cold water. Wrap the dough and chill it for thirty minutes. Roll it out and line a 23 centimetre tart tin, prick the base with a fork and bake it blind at 180 degrees Celsius for fifteen minutes with baking beans, then five minutes more without them. For the filling, whisk together four eggs, 150 grams of sugar, the zest and juice of three lemons and 150 millilitres of double cream. Lower the oven to 150 degrees, pour the filling into the pastry case and bake for about thirty minutes, until it is just set with a slight wobble in the centre. Leave the tart to cool, then chill it for at least two hours. Serve in thin slices with fresh raspberries.
label: dessert

text: Blueberry Muffins. Heat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius and place twelve paper cases in a muffin tin. In one bowl mix 250 grams of plain flour, 150 grams of sugar, two teaspoons of baking powder and a pinch of salt. In another bowl whisk two eggs with 120 millilitres of milk, 100 millilitres of sunflower oil and the grated zest of one lemon. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ones and stir briefly with a fork; the batter should remain lumpy, because overmixing makes muffins tough. Gently fold in 150 grams of fresh or frozen blueberries. Spoon the batter into the cases, filling them almost to the top, and sprinkle each muffin with a little demerara sugar for a crunchy crust. Bake for twenty minutes, until risen, golden and a skewer inserted in the middle comes out clean. Cool for a few minutes in the tin and serve warm with butter or a cup of tea.
label: dessert

text: Apple Crumble Pie. Peel, core and slice five large cooking apples and place them in a saucepan with 60 grams of brown sugar, a teaspoon of ground cinnamon, a pinch of nutmeg and two tablespoons of water. Cook over a low heat for about eight minutes, until the apples begin to soften but still hold their shape. Transfer the fruit to a buttered baking dish. For the crumble topping, rub 100 grams of cold butter into 180 grams of flour with your fingertips, then stir in 80 grams of demerara sugar and a handful of rolled oats. Scatter the crumble evenly over the apples without pressing it down. Bake at 190 degrees Celsius for thirty to thirty-five minutes, until the topping is crisp and golden and the fruit juices are bubbling at the edges. Let the dessert rest for ten minutes, then serve it warm with vanilla custard or a scoop of ice cream.
label: dessert

text: Chocolate Brownies. Line a square baking tin with parchment and preheat the oven to 170 degrees Celsius. Melt 185 grams of butter and 185 grams of dark chocolate together in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring until smooth, then let the mixture cool slightly. In a large bowl, whisk three eggs with 275 grams of caster sugar for about five minutes until thick, pale and doubled in volume. Pour in the melted chocolate and fold it through carefully. Sift over 85 grams of plain flour and 40 grams of cocoa powder and fold again until no streaks remain. Stir in a handful of chopped walnuts or white chocolate pieces if you like. Pour the batter into the tin and bake for twenty-five minutes; the top should be shiny and crackly while the middle stays fudgy. Cool completely in the tin before cutting into sixteen squares.
label: dessert

text: Strawberry Cheesecake. Crush 200 grams of digestive biscuits into fine crumbs and mix them with 80 grams of melted butter. Press the mixture firmly into the base of a springform tin and chill it while you make the filling. Beat 600 grams of full-fat cream cheese with 100 grams of icing sugar and a teaspoon of vanilla until smooth. In another bowl whip 300 millilitres of double cream to soft peaks, then fold it into the cheese mixture. Spread the filling over the biscuit base and level the surface with a spatula. Cover and refrigerate the cheesecake for at least six hours, or ideally overnight, until firm. Shortly before serving, hull and halve 300 grams of fresh strawberries and toss them with a tablespoon of sugar and a squeeze of lemon juice. Remove the cheesecake from the tin, arrange the glossy berries on top and cut it with a knife dipped in hot water.
label: dessert

text: Cinnamon Rolls. Warm 240 millilitres of milk and dissolve a sachet of dried yeast and 50 grams of sugar in it. Add one egg and 60 grams of melted butter, then mix in 450 grams of strong flour and a teaspoon of salt to form a soft dough. Knead for ten minutes until smooth and elastic, place it in an oiled bowl, cover and leave it to rise for an hour. Roll the dough into a large rectangle and spread it with 80 grams of soft butter mixed with 100 grams of brown sugar and two tablespoons of cinnamon. Roll it up tightly from the long side and cut it into twelve slices. Arrange the rolls in a greased tin and let them prove for another thirty minutes. Bake at 180 degrees Celsius for twenty-five minutes. While they are still warm, drizzle the rolls with a glaze of cream cheese, icing sugar and a splash of milk.
label: dessert

text: French Macarons. Sift 100 grams of ground almonds with 100 grams of icing sugar twice to remove any lumps. In a clean bowl, whisk two egg whites until foamy, then gradually add 90 grams of caster sugar and keep whisking until the meringue is stiff and glossy. Add a few drops of food colouring if you want pastel shells. Fold the almond mixture into the meringue in three additions, pressing the batter against the side of the bowl until it flows slowly like lava. Transfer it to a piping bag and pipe small rounds onto baking trays lined with parchment. Tap the trays firmly on the work surface to release air bubbles, then leave the shells to dry for thirty minutes until a skin forms. Bake at 150 degrees Celsius for fourteen minutes. Once cool, sandwich pairs of shells together with chocolate ganache or buttercream and store them in the fridge for a day before eating.
label: dessert

text: Tiramisu. Brew 300 millilitres of strong espresso, stir in two tablespoons of coffee liqueur and leave it to cool. Separate four eggs. Whisk the yolks with 80 grams of sugar until thick and pale, then beat in 500 grams of mascarpone until smooth and creamy. In another bowl, whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the mascarpone cream. Quickly dip about twenty savoiardi sponge fingers into the coffee one at a time, so they absorb the liquid without falling apart, and arrange half of them in a single layer in a serving dish. Spread half of the cream over the biscuits, then repeat with another layer of soaked sponge fingers and the remaining cream. Smooth the top, cover the dish and chill the dessert for at least four hours so the flavours can develop. Just before serving, dust generously with cocoa powder through a fine sieve.
label: dessert

text: Roast Chicken with Garlic and Herbs. Take a whole chicken of about 1.6 kilograms out of the fridge thirty minutes before cooking and pat the skin dry with kitchen paper. Preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius. Mix 50 grams of soft butter with four crushed garlic cloves, chopped thyme, rosemary and plenty of salt and black pepper. Carefully loosen the skin over the breast and push half of the herb butter underneath, then rub the rest over the outside of the bird. Place a halved lemon and a few sprigs of herbs inside the cavity. Put the chicken in a roasting tin on a bed of sliced onions and carrots and roast it for about one hour and twenty minutes, basting with the juices halfway through. The chicken is done when the juices from the thickest part of the thigh run clear. Rest it under foil for fifteen minutes, then carve and serve with the roasted vegetables and pan gravy.
label: savoury

text: Pan-Seared Salmon with Lemon Butter. Pat four salmon fillets dry and season them on both sides with salt and freshly ground pepper. Heat a tablespoon of olive oil in a heavy frying pan over a medium-high heat until it shimmers. Lay the fillets in the pan skin side down and press them gently with a spatula for the first few seconds so the skin stays flat and becomes crisp. Cook without moving them for about four minutes, until the flesh turns opaque two thirds of the way up. Turn the fish over and cook for one to two minutes more, depending on thickness. Remove the salmon to warm plates. Lower the heat, add 40 grams of butter, a crushed garlic clove, the juice of half a lemon and a spoonful of capers, and swirl the pan until the sauce foams. Spoon the lemon butter over the fish and serve with new potatoes and steamed green beans.
label: savoury

text: Beef Stew with Root Vegetables. Cut 800 grams of braising beef into large chunks, season them and toss them in two tablespoons of flour. Brown the meat in batches in a heavy casserole with a little oil, then set it aside. In the same pot, soften two chopped onions, two carrots and two sticks of celery for ten minutes. Add two crushed garlic cloves and a tablespoon of tomato paste and cook for one minute. Return the beef to the pot, pour in 250 millilitres of red wine and let it bubble for a couple of minutes, scraping the bottom to release the browned bits. Add 600 millilitres of beef stock, two bay leaves and a few sprigs of thyme. Cover and simmer gently on the lowest heat for two hours, then add cubed potatoes and parsnips and cook for another forty minutes, until the meat is tender and the sauce has thickened. Serve with crusty bread.
label: savoury

text: Bruschetta with Tomatoes and Basil. Dice six ripe plum tomatoes, discarding most of the seeds, and place them in a bowl. Add one finely chopped shallot, a crushed garlic clove, a handful of torn basil leaves, two tablespoons of good extra virgin olive oil and a teaspoon of balsamic vinegar. Season with sea salt and black pepper, stir gently and leave the mixture to marinate for fifteen minutes while the flavours blend. Meanwhile, cut a crusty baguette or ciabatta into slices about one and a half centimetres thick. Brush both sides lightly with olive oil and toast the slices under a hot grill or on a griddle pan until they are golden and marked. While the bread is still warm, rub each slice with the cut side of a halved garlic clove. Pile the tomato topping onto the toasts just before serving, so the bread stays crunchy, and finish with a drizzle of oil.
label: savoury

text: Shrimp Garlic Skewers. Peel and devein 500 grams of large raw prawns, leaving the tails on. In a bowl, combine three tablespoons of olive oil, four finely chopped garlic cloves, the zest and juice of a lime, a teaspoon of smoked paprika, a pinch of chilli flakes and some salt. Add the prawns, toss them until well coated and marinate them in the fridge for twenty minutes, but not longer, because the citrus will start to cook the seafood. If you are using wooden skewers, soak them in water for half an hour so they do not burn. Thread the prawns onto the skewers, alternating them with pieces of red pepper and onion. Cook them on a hot barbecue or griddle for about two minutes on each side, until the prawns are pink and slightly charred. Sprinkle them with chopped coriander and serve with lime wedges as a starter or party snack.
label: savoury

text: Stuffed Mushrooms with Bacon. Remove the stalks from sixteen medium chestnut mushrooms and chop the stalks finely. Fry four rashers of streaky bacon in a dry pan until crisp, then lift them out, chop them and keep the fat in the pan. Cook one small chopped onion and the mushroom stalks in the bacon fat for five minutes until soft, add a crushed garlic clove and cook for one minute more. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the bacon, 100 grams of cream cheese, 40 grams of grated parmesan, a handful of breadcrumbs and some chopped parsley. Season with pepper. Arrange the mushroom caps on a lined baking tray, fill each one generously with the stuffing and sprinkle with a little extra parmesan. Bake at 190 degrees Celsius for about eighteen minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the tops are golden. Serve warm as an appetiser.
label: savoury

text: Grilled Pork Chops with Mustard Sauce. Season four thick bone-in pork chops with salt, pepper and a little dried sage, and let them stand at room temperature for twenty minutes. Heat a griddle or heavy frying pan until very hot and brush the chops with oil. Cook them for four to five minutes on each side, then hold them on their fatty edge for a minute to render and crisp the fat. The pork should reach an internal temperature of 63 degrees Celsius. Transfer the chops to a plate and rest them under foil. To make the sauce, lower the heat, add a knob of butter and a finely chopped shallot to the pan and cook until soft. Pour in 100 millilitres of white wine and let it reduce by half, then stir in 150 millilitres of cream and a tablespoon of wholegrain mustard. Simmer until slightly thickened and pour over the chops.
label: savoury

text: Fish Tacos with Cabbage Slaw. Cut 500 grams of firm white fish, such as cod or haddock, into finger-sized strips. Mix a teaspoon each of ground cumin, chilli powder and garlic powder with some salt, and coat the fish with the spice mix. For the slaw, finely shred a quarter of a red cabbage, grate one carrot and toss them with lime juice, a pinch of salt and chopped coriander. Make a quick sauce by stirring together sour cream, mayonnaise and a little chipotle paste. Heat oil in a frying pan and cook the fish strips for two to three minutes on each side, until golden and just flaking. Warm small corn tortillas in a dry pan for a few seconds on each side. To assemble, place a spoonful of slaw on each tortilla, top with pieces of fish, drizzle with the smoky sauce and add slices of avocado. Serve immediately with lime wedges.
label: savoury

text: Lamb Meatballs in Tomato Sauce. Combine 500 grams of minced lamb in a bowl with one grated onion, two crushed garlic cloves, a teaspoon of ground cumin, a teaspoon of coriander, a handful of chopped mint, one egg and 40 grams of breadcrumbs. Season well and mix with your hands, then roll the mixture into about twenty walnut-sized balls. Brown the meatballs in a large frying pan with a little oil, turning them until coloured on all sides, and set them aside. In the same pan, fry a sliced onion until soft, add a pinch of cinnamon and a teaspoon of paprika, then pour in two tins of chopped tomatoes and a splash of water. Simmer the sauce for ten minutes, return the meatballs to the pan and cook gently for another fifteen minutes, until they are cooked through. Scatter with crumbled feta and fresh herbs and serve with couscous or warm flatbread.
label: savoury

text: Smoked Salmon Canapés. Cut slices of dark rye or pumpernickel bread into small squares or rounds using a pastry cutter, allowing about twenty pieces. In a bowl, beat 150 grams of cream cheese with a tablespoon of lemon juice, a teaspoon of creamed horseradish, chopped fresh dill and some black pepper until smooth and spreadable. Spread a thin layer of the cheese mixture over each piece of bread. Cut 200 grams of smoked salmon into strips and fold or roll a piece loosely on top of each canapé so that it looks generous. Garnish each one with a small sprig of dill, a few capers or a tiny slice of cucumber, and finish with a little lemon zest. Arrange the canapés on a serving platter, cover them with cling film and keep them in the fridge for no longer than two hours before serving, so the bread does not become soggy. They make an elegant cold appetiser.
label: savoury
